key_insight: Bitumen liberation is driven by surface shear exceeding a critical threshold, with faster release at higher particle Reynolds numbers and smaller lump diameters.
engineering_relevance: A shear-based predictive model could guide oil sands hydrotransport operating conditions to improve bitumen recovery.
method: 3D Eulerian–Eulerian CFD with k–ω SST turbulence modeling.
Six cases spanning 4–5 cm lump diameters and particle Reynolds numbers of 2000–4000.
Semi-empirical liberation model based on shear-driven detachment.
evidence_signal: The proposed model was validated against experimental liberation data, with reported error below 8.3%.
watch_item: Applicability beyond the studied lump sizes and Reynolds numbers requires further validation.
paper_title: Numerical Investigations on Bitumen Liberation from Oil Sands Lump
